messages:
incident-bot: URGENT: Increased 5xx rate observed for ALB in euc2 (ALB-prod-euc2) — ~40% 502/504s, many connection resets. Triggered by 2 consecutive anomaly windows. Paging on-call for euc2. https://pagerduty.example/incident/INC12345 :rotating_light:

maya-sre: acked — I'm on it, taking primary. pinging network to check for AZ flaps.

sam-ops: oncall here, joining. quick check: ALB target-group health shows ~30% unhealthy across targets in euc2b. no config changes in last 24h.

kevin-net: looking at VPC flow logs and NLB metrics. Seeing a spike in TCP RST from proxy layer to backend pool starting 02:04 UTC. Could be Envoy upstream resets or backend oom.

maya-sre: running curl against the ALB from us-east test runner to reproduce:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.example/health || true
*   Trying 10.0.5.23:443...
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.example (10.0.5.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: 
* Received reset from peer
* Closing connection 0
```

sam-ops: grabbing envoy logs from one of the edges in euc2b — tail below (redacted):
```
[2026-07-12T02:05:08Z] envoy upstream reset: CONNECTION_TERMINATION, downstream_remote:10.0.1.45
[2026-07-12T02:05:09Z] healthcheck fail, marking host unhealthy
[2026-07-12T02:05:10Z] TLSv1.2 handshake failed: unexpected eof
```

kevin-net: AWS console shows an AZ-level networking disruption in euc2b; Cloud provider incident id: AWS-2026-euc2b-net-amt. There's a known issue with an overloaded transit gateway peer in that AZ causing packet drops. Opening support case to confirm.

maya-sre: mitigation idea: shift traffic away from euc2b to euc2a and euc2c, and bring up spare targets in euc2a. Initiating gradual traffic shift via ALB weighted-target override.

sam-ops: doing target registration now — adding 3 warm standby instances in euc2a and health-checking.

deploy-bot: auto-rollout-safe-check: traffic shift will not trigger deploys. 2/3 warm instances passed healthchecks (10s). Proceeding to update endpoint weights.

maya-sre: weight update applied — shifting ~70% of traffic off euc2b over 90s. Monitoring 5xx rate.

kevin-net: Route53 records unaffected; however there was a transient route table propagation delay for euc2b that may have contributed. Confirmed from provider: packet loss window 02:03–02:09 UTC.

jules-cs: customer-impact note: CS monitoring shows elevated error rates for EU customers, particularly mobile SDKs. We have 17 customer error reports so far, estimated 6% of EU requests affected in last 10m. Escalating to CS lead.

maya-sre: after shift, 5xx rate dropped from 40% to ~3% within 3 minutes. Connection resets ceased for the traffic now routed to euc2a/c. euc2b still showing health flaps — keeping it out of rotation.

sam-ops: placing euc2b targets in standby and disabling autoscale triggers for that AZ to avoid churn.

kevin-net: AWS confirms they are mitigating the transit gateway peer; ETA unknown. Recommend leaving failover config in place and monitor for reattachment.

maya-sre: summary for now: impact mitigated by traffic shift, partial customer impact (mobile SDKs, ~6% EU requests). oncall handoff: sam-ops will remain until euc2b is healthy or AWS confirms fix, then we'll reintroduce with slow bake. Creating incident ticket and adding action items: root-cause (provider AZ networking), proof of impact, restoration plan, and postmortem owner.

sam-ops: taking 1h follow-up, will update PD and tag postmortem. leaving this thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
